columns.description: The fields shown, in order. Left out, the schedule's usual ones. labels.description: The words the table is written with, by field (the heading of its column), and 'total' (the last row) and 'none' (what stands for no material or no type). Left out, English ones.

size.description: Text size in mm. Defaults to 200.

source.description: The id of the page whose contents it counts. Defaults to the page it is on.

totals.description: Whether a last row adds up the columns that can be added up. Defaults to true.

rowsPerBlock.description: At most this many rows of things counted one under the other: the next ones go into a block beside it, with the headings again, and so on, the total at the end of the last. Left out, all in one block.

only.description: The rows shown, by their keys; the others are left out of the table and its total, and what comes on the plan later is not shown. Keys: objects 'component:<id>', or for a parametric object 'parametric:' then its kind and every one of its parameters, defaults filled in, as JSON with its keys in order ('parametric:arch.radiator {"length":800,...}': a model with other parameters is another row); floors 'material:<id>' ('material:' for the floors of no material); rooms 'room:<id>'; walls 'material:<id>' and the thickness in mm, as 'material:brick 200' ('material: 200' for the default material); openings the kind, then width and height in metres, as 'arch.door 0.9 2.1', whatever the table's units; controls 'control:<id>' of the switch. decimal.description: The decimal separator of its numbers, in place of the drawing's "settings". Left out (as it should be), the drawing's.

system.description: 'imperial' gives lengths in feet, areas in square feet, volumes in cubic feet and thicknesses in inches, in place of the drawing's "settings". Left out (as it should be), the drawing's.

language.description: The language code its rows are named in where they take a name from an extension, as "fr".

oneOf.description: An elevation or a section: a cut along its line on the plan, from a to b, seen from the right of that line (as it runs from a to b, which is below a line drawn from left to right, since Y grows downward), so that a is on the left of the view, looking beyond it up to depth; drawn from the plan each time it is drawn, at (x, y), the point of the floor under a, heights going up from there. What the line crosses is drawn cut through (walls, above and below the doors and windows they are cut at); beyond it, up to depth, the faces turned towards it with their doors, windows and what is fixed on them at its height, the furniture, and the walls in the way. A line whose far side (depth beyond it) lies on the face of a wall makes an elevation of that wall, and follows the wall when the wall changes: usually 1000 in front of the face, with depth 1000. One across the plan makes a section. The line is shown on the plan in the editor, to place it, and never printed. Moving the view moves where it is drawn; moving it with the walls it looks at moves its line too. It holds what is drawn on it as its children (dimension, text, annotation, line, polyline, rect, ellipse), in its own coordinates: x along its line from a, y up from its floor (negative), in mm of the plan, drawn at (x, y) and its scale, so that a dimension says the real length.

items.description: A non-destructive change to how a node is drawn; the node itself is not altered. 'crop' shows only what is inside the rectangle that starts at its frame and has params.width and params.height.

meta.description: Free-form data for extensions and tools.

kind.description: Parametric kind registered by an extension, e.g. 'arch.stair'.

props.description: Parameters of the kind. Missing ones use the kind defaults.

z.description: How high above the floor it is, in mm: for an object fixed on a wall, to its centre (a socket's or a switch's height) unless its kind measures it to its underside; for anything else, to its underside (a raised unit, a shelf). Left out, its kind's usual height for an object fixed on a wall, else on the floor. The plan writes it only with showHeight.

showHeight.description: For an object fixed on a wall: its height above the floor is written beside it on the plan, as electrical plans do.

oneOf.description: An object generated from parameters by an extension. Unknown kinds are preserved and drawn as a placeholder.

additionalProperties.description: All coordinates and lengths are millimetres. X grows to the right, Y grows downward.

nodes.description: Every node by id, as a flat map. The tree is expressed by each node's "parent" and "order".

info.description: What the drawing says about itself, shown in the title block of every sheet: the project (the document name when not given), the client, the address of the site (lines separated by a line break), the author.

settings.description: How the drawing writes its numbers (the floor areas of its rooms, its tables of quantities, its dimensions) and lays out the title blocks of its sheets. Left out, in metric with a decimal point, the block in the corner.

system.description: 'imperial': areas in square feet, and the lengths, volumes and thicknesses of tables of quantities in feet and inches. Defaults to 'metric' (square metres, metres).

decimal.description: The decimal separator of the areas, tables and dimensions. Defaults to '.'.

titleBlock.description: How the title blocks of every sheet are laid out, the same throughout the set. Left out, in the corner. What each sheet shows is its own ("titleBlock" of a paper).

layout.description: 'corner' (the default): a block of values in the bottom right corner. 'strip': a column down the right edge of the sheet, as US sheets have it, each entry under its caption, the project at the top, the revisions under it and the sheet title and number at the bottom.

labels.description: The captions of the strip, by entry (project, client, address, sheet, page, author, scale, format, date, number, revisions). Left out, English ones; an empty one is not drawn.

grid.description: The grid the editor shows and snaps to, from the origin. Left out, the grid changes with the zoom (1, 5, 10, 50, 100 mm…), every tenth line darker. It is never printed or exported.

spacing.description: How far apart the main lines of the grid are, in mm: 910 for the Japanese module.

divisions.description: Into how many parts the finer lines divide each square of the main ones: 2 gives lines every 455 mm between those every 910 mm. Defaults to 1, no finer lines.
